question: New job: part SM-107 (Sensor mount plate, compact), material 6061-T6 aluminum, qty 50, 6 features, deepest pocket 10 mm, 6 holes, plate 70 cm2. Using ONLY Keewano history: (1) which toolpath strategies should the CAM search try first for this part (rank by simulated cycle time on the most similar past parts, especially by pocket depth; drop strategies that failed verification or never win), (2) which supplier to buy a missing aluminum blank from (delivered price vs lead days from past quotes), (3) which step of the order is the bottleneck (StepSeconds), (4) before vs after: agent programming time vs the manual estimate, best vs manual-baseline machine time. Then call final_decision.

answer.supplier_reason: Its delivered price was the lowest on both parts it quoted. SM-101: $266.75-$299.40 vs Pacific Metals Supply $334.70-$401.80. FTC-10: $47.60 vs $86.70. Bay's lead time was 2 days. Pacific delivered in 0-1 days on SM-101 but cost about 25% more. Pick Pacific only if the blank is needed within 2 days.
answer.before_after: Programming: the shop's manual estimate is 14400 s (4 h). The agent took 2-4 s on similar native SM-10x jobs, and SM-101 averaged 63.8 s across its 5 runs, which include Fusion. Machine time, manual baseline vs best: SM-101 at 8 mm averaged 1282 s (21:22) vs 267.4 s (4:27), 78.4% saved. SM-103 at 8 mm was 1937 vs 232 s, 88%. SM-106 at 12 mm was 1855 vs 218 s, 88%. SM-102 at 14 mm was 1504 vs 199 s, 87%.
answer.summary: For SM-107 (10 mm pocket), try adaptive-so45-ap2D first because it won at 12 and 14 mm. Next try conventional-so60-ap1D, which won at 5 and 8 mm, then adaptive-L3.0-D20 as the Fusion fallback. Expected cycle is about 3:20, against 20-32 min for a manual-style program. Buy the missing 6061-T6 blank from Bay Alloy & Steel, the cheapest delivered option at 2 days' lead. The slow step is the supplier phone calls (dial.supplier_call, 885 s in total, up to 279 s per call); CAM programming itself takes seconds.
